Those who strike their cheeks, tear clothes, cry the slogans of ignorance, wail or shave their hair are not of the Prophet's people, as Abu Musa told his wife.
The Prophet stopped Umm Salama's planned mourning, yet wept at his daughter's dying child and at the sick Sa'd b. Ubada, saying Allah punishes for the tongue, not tears.
When Umar was wounded and Hafsa and Suhaib lamented him, he reminded them that the Prophet said the dead is punished because of the living's weeping over him.
Ibn Umar taught the dead is punished for his family's lamenting; Aisha replied the Prophet said it of an unbeliever or a dead Jew, citing that none bears another's burden.
One lamented is punished for it; wailing is a pre-Islamic habit, an unrepentant wailing woman will stand at Resurrection in pitch garments; the Prophet forbade Ja'far's women to lament.
Women pledged to the Prophet not to wail, though only five kept it, with one exception for Umm Atiyya; women were forbidden, though not absolutely, to follow the bier.
The Prophet had his daughter Zainab washed an odd number of times, right side first, camphor in the last wash, hair in three plaits, and gave his undergarment for her.
The Prophet told the women washing his daughter's body to begin on the right side and with the parts washed in ablution.
Mus'ab, killed at Uhud, had too short a cloak, grass covering his feet; the Prophet was shrouded in three white cotton sheets, no shirt or turban; shroud the dead well.
The Prophet told people to hasten with a funeral: a good person is brought sooner to good, and from an evil one they rid themselves.
Attending a funeral until the prayer earns one qirat and until burial two, each like Uhud; Ibn Umar, after Aisha confirmed Abu Huraira's report, said they had missed many qirats.
Paradise is certain for a dead person people praise, Hell for one they condemn, as they are Allah's witnesses; a believer's death relieves him, a wicked one's relieves others.
The Prophet announced the Negus's death on the day he died, told them to ask pardon for their brother, and led the prayer over him in rows with four takbirs.
The Prophet prayed with four takbirs over graves after burial, including the mosque sweeper's, whose death he was not told of; Zaid once said five takbirs, as the Prophet had.
Stand when a bier passes, even a Jew's, until it passes or is set down, nor sit while following it; Ali said the Prophet stood at first, then later sat.
Leading the funeral prayer for a woman who died in childbirth, the Prophet stood level with the middle of her body.
After Ibn Dahdah's funeral prayer the Prophet rode back on an unsaddled horse as people walked and ran around him, and spoke of fruit bunches in Paradise for Ibn Dahdah.
Sa'd asked for a niche grave with bricks like the Prophet's, where a red cloth was placed; the Prophet ordered graves levelled and images obliterated.
The Prophet forbade plastering graves, building over them, sitting on them or praying towards them, saying that sitting on live coals is better than sitting on a grave.
Criticised for having Sa'd b. Abu Waqqas's bier brought into the mosque for prayer, Aisha said the Prophet had offered the funeral prayer of Suhail b. Baida' in the mosque.
The Prophet went by night to al-Baqi' to greet its dead and ask forgiveness for them, as Gabriel commanded, Aisha secretly following, and taught a greeting for graveyards.
Allowed to visit his mother's grave but not to seek forgiveness for her, the Prophet wept, and permitted visiting graves, which recall death, and keeping sacrificial meat.
The Prophet did not offer the funeral prayer over a man who had killed himself with a broad-headed arrow.
A pilgrim in ihram whose camel broke his neck is washed with lote-tree water, shrouded in his two cloths, unperfumed, head and face uncovered, to be raised pronouncing Talbiya.
